sections.title: Healthy habits

q.prompt: Which word means “good for your body”?

options.fb: “vegetables” means plants we eat, like carrots and peas.
“exercise” means moving your body to keep fit.

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 3. In this lesson: Healthy habits.
Give advice with ‘should’ and ‘shouldn't’.
Here are some new words. Healthy. Good for your body. Exercise.
Moving your body to keep fit. Vegetables. Plants we eat, like carrots and peas.
Listen and say them. healthy
exercise
vegetables.
And some more words. Sugar. Something sweet in cakes and fizzy drinks. Rest.
Relax and stop working. Germs. Tiny living things that can make you ill.
Listen and say them. sugar
rest
germs.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: good for your body?
Now some grammar: should and shouldn't. Use ‘should’ to give good advice.
Use ‘shouldn't’ for things that are not a good idea.
For example: You should drink water. For example: You shouldn't eat lots of sweets.
Now listen, and read along. Dr Kim's tips for a healthy week. Hello! I'm Dr Kim.
Here are my tips for a healthy week. You should eat fruit and vegetables every day.
They help your body grow. You should drink lots of water.
You shouldn't have fizzy drinks every day, because they have lots of sugar.
You should exercise for one hour every day. Ride a bike, dance or play football!
And you should sleep for about ten hours every night. Rest is important too!
Another question. The video will stop. Who is giving the tips?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like healthy, exercise, vegetables.
You practised should and shouldn't. And you read Dr Kim's tips for a healthy week.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

sections.title: How often?

q.prompt: How many children did Class 3B ask?

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 3. In this lesson: How often?
Use adverbs of frequency and read a simple survey report.
Here are some new words. Always. Every time. Usually. Most times. Sometimes.
Some of the time. Listen and say them. always
usually
sometimes.
And some more words. Never. Not at any time. Survey.
Asking many people the same questions. Result. What you find out at the end.
Listen and say them. never
survey
result.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: every time?
Now some grammar: Adverbs of frequency.
Adverbs of frequency go before most verbs but after ‘be’.
For example: I always eat breakfast. For example: She is never late.
Now listen, and read along. Class 3B's breakfast survey. Class 3B did a survey.
We asked 20 children, ‘How often do you eat breakfast?’ Here are the results.
12 children always eat breakfast. 5 children usually eat breakfast.
2 children sometimes eat breakfast. 1 child never eats breakfast.
Most children in our class eat breakfast.
This is good, because breakfast gives you energy for the morning.
Another question. The video will stop. How many children did Class 3B ask?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like always, usually, sometimes.
You practised adverbs of frequency. And you read Class 3B's breakfast survey.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
